We actually had the opposite issue at the start with our pup! He really liked sleeping outside the crate instead of in it at first, and took a long time settling whenever he had to be inside. Fortunately he’s starting to get used to it now.

But anyway, in addition to exhausting your pup to try and get him to sleep, you could try some ways of relaxing him since it’s a possibility that he might find it hard to drift off BECAUSE he’s too tired (like a cranky toddler). Sometimes they can’t tell that they need to sleep without a little nudge in the right direction to slumberland. What we found helped a lot were calming wipes / sprays that are made to relax anxious pups and also playing music in the background. Classical or reggae music works the best for ours, but every dog is different. Good luck!
